output.contract_title: Vendor Procurement Agreement with Enterprise Partner 019 LLC

clauses.clause_text: Customer shall pay all undisputed invoice amounts within thirty (30) days of invoice date.
Vendor will endeavor to report security incidents in a reasonable and commercially practical timeframe.
Liability shall be determined in accordance with applicable general trade customs.
Either party may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon providing thirty (30) days prior written notice.
This Agreement renews on an annual basis unless either party gives notice of non-renewal at least 30 days prior.

extraction_notes: Document extracted once for downstream policy comparison

mandatory_requirements.description: Vendor must notify customer of any security breach within 48 hours of discovery.
Data must be encrypted in transit using TLS 1.3 and at rest using AES-256.

deviations.supporting_evidence: Mapping status is 'partially_satisfied' indicating the clause does not fully meet the 48‑hour breach notification requirement; the contract language allows up to 72 hours before notification.
deviations.recommended_remediation: Amend clause CLS-0019-DATA to require notification of any security breach within 48 hours of discovery, with explicit penalties for non‑compliance.

deviations.supporting_evidence: Mapping status is 'unaddressed' and no clause is linked to REQ-SEC-02, meaning the contract contains no provisions for TLS 1.3 encryption in transit or AES‑256 encryption at rest.
deviations.recommended_remediation: Insert a new data‑protection clause that mandates encryption of all data in transit using TLS 1.3 and encryption at rest using AES‑256, and include compliance monitoring and audit rights.

risk_findings.ambiguity_description: The term "undisputed invoice amounts" is undefined, leaving uncertainty about what constitutes a dispute and how disputed amounts are handled.
The phrase "reasonable and commercially practical timeframe" provides no concrete deadline for breach notification, creating potential delays in incident response.
Liability is to be determined "in accordance with applicable general trade customs," which is vague and may lead to unpredictable liability exposure.

inconsistencies.description: Liability clause references "applicable general trade customs" without defining a monetary cap or scope, creating ambiguity and potential conflict with any statutory limitation or other contractual obligations.

Data breach notification clause uses vague language "reasonable and commercially practical timeframe," which may be interpreted inconsistently with industry standards or regulatory requirements for prompt reporting.

Termination for convenience (30 days notice) and renewal notice (30 days prior to renewal) operate on overlapping timelines; a party could terminate the agreement within the renewal notice window, rendering the renewal provision ineffective and creating a procedural conflict.
